title: Microsoft Expects 3,000 or Fewer Takers for Exit Offer Open to 60,000 Staff
excerpt: The voluntary offer covers staff in India, the US, Canada and the UK at level 70 and below; India employees are reported to have until December 1 to decide.
body:
• Microsoft expects 3,000 or fewer employees to accept its new Voluntary Exit Offer, even though about 60,000 employees — roughly a quarter of its 223,000 workforce — are eligible.
  • The offer, announced October 26, covers eligible staff at level 70 and below in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States.
  • Microsoft has about 23,000 employees in India; how many of them are eligible is not yet clear, and eligible India staff are reported to have until December 1 to decide.
  • The India package is understood to resemble standard severance — a month's base salary per completed year of service, plus health insurance and career transition services — though Microsoft has not published the terms.

Microsoft expects very few takers for its new Voluntary Exit Offer. The offer, announced on October 26, is open to about 60,000 eligible employees, but the company expects 3,000 or fewer — roughly 5% of those eligible — to accept, a spokesperson told Business Insider, as reported by People Matters on October 30. Chief Financial Officer Amy Hood made the same point internally.

"Our intent is to offer employees agency if they choose to leave the company on their own terms. We expect very few people to select this offer because of the growth opportunities here at Microsoft."

— Amy Hood, Chief Financial Officer, Microsoft

What was offered

The Voluntary Exit Offer was introduced on October 26 by Amy Coleman, Microsoft's Executive Vice President and Chief People Officer, in a post on the official Microsoft blog. It is open to eligible employees in participating organisations in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States, at level 70 and below — a band that, as TechCrunch put it, runs to the vice-president level and below. Microsoft confirmed to TechCrunch that about 60,000 employees are eligible, out of a total workforce of 223,000 at the end of June. Coleman wrote that the offer "gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support," and that it builds on the company's Voluntary Retirement Program earlier this year. Unlike that retirement programme — open to about 8,750 US employees, of whom roughly 30% accepted — the exit offer carries no age or length-of-service requirement.

Microsoft's blog does not publish the severance terms, a headcount for acceptances, or a deadline. Bloomberg, cited by TechCrunch, reported that participating divisions include Xbox, Windows, Copilot and Finance, while data centres, sales and marketing are excluded. Microsoft has said the voluntary exits are not a replacement for layoffs; it announced about 4,800 job cuts in July, and departures under the offer are expected by the end of 2026.

What it means for India staff

Microsoft employs about 23,000 people in India, but there is no immediate clarity on how many of them are eligible, PTI reported. It is learnt that eligible employees in India have until December 1 to decide. The package is understood to be similar to a standard severance arrangement, including one month's base salary for each completed year of service, plus health insurance and career transition services — terms reported by PTI, not published by Microsoft.

Alongside the offer, a Microsoft spokesperson pointed to continued investment in India: the company says it is on track to equip 20 million people across India with AI skills by 2030 and has committed $20.5 billion between 2025 and 2029 across cloud and AI infrastructure, skilling and operations. For India staff weighing the offer, the practical questions — eligibility, the December 1 deadline, and the exact package — are being answered individually: eligible employees received their offer details by email from the company.
